reference: GNU coreutils 9.7 cat, invoked by system Bash on the reference side; stderr is compared byte for byte after the shell's script-line prefix is removed.
coverage: Guest compatibility pass 6 (G90): GNU diagnostic wording for operand and usage errors.
exclusions: Only diagnostics are covered here; the reviewed suite in suites/ covers ordinary operation.

cases.purpose: G90: a read error names the operand as GNU does ('cat: d: Is a directory', '-' for standard input), and an open error keeps the bare name. The shell's script-line prefix is stripped so the case holds before and after the builtin-prefix change.
cases.script:
mkdir d
printf 'kept\n' > f
{ cat d || echo rc=$?; } 2>err
{ cat < d || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
{ cat nosuch f || echo rc=$?; } 2>>err
sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //' err >&2
rm err
